display.purpose: Profile names at hero scale. The UV spotlight moment. Outfit Black (900) — geometric with personality, confident and well-made.

headline.purpose: Page headers, card titles, modal headings. Outfit ExtraBold (800).

title.purpose: Section subheadings, panel headers. Inter Semibold — the transition to the sans register.

body.purpose: All prose, form copy, link descriptions, bio text. Inter Regular. Max line length 65ch.

label.purpose: Field labels, nav links, button text, badges. Inter Medium, uppercase, tracked. Used everywhere Inter appears as UI chrome.

shadows.name: amber-focus-glow
shadows.purpose: Focus rings on amber-coded interactive elements: primary buttons, amber-bordered inputs, link cards.

shadows.name: laser-focus-glow
shadows.purpose: Focus rings on laser-coded elements. The violet flash — use at most twice per viewport.

shadows.name: avatar-halo-resting
shadows.purpose: Profile avatar in resting state. Constant dim violet ambient — the UV that's always on.

shadows.name: avatar-halo-active
shadows.purpose: Profile avatar on hover or featured position. The UV spotlight expanding.

shadows.name: panel-lift
shadows.purpose: Subtle inner-top highlight on raised surface components. Ambient bounce in a cool dark space.

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: Default easing for all transitions. Fast out, nothing lingers.

motion.name: duration-instant
motion.purpose: Micro-interactions: checkbox toggles, radio selections, immediate feedback.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Hover state changes: background shifts, border-color, color transitions.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: Element entrances, avatar halo expansion, panel reveals, stagger beats.

motion.name: duration-exit
motion.purpose: Exit transitions — always faster than entrances.

motion.name: stagger-step
motion.purpose: Delay increment between staggered list items. A 10-item link list completes in under 600ms.

motion.name: laser-pulse
motion.purpose: Optional subtle pulse animation on the avatar laser halo. Use only on the public profile landing — never in admin/studio. Must be disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Desktop → full layout with preview pane

narrative.overview:
A black room where pups and furs dance under UV and green laser light, leather gear absorbing the dark, neon suits cutting the air, the bass punching through your chest. Two things are true at once: this is a leather community and a rave community. The surface is void-black. The warmth of polished amber hardware glows against it. Above that, a single electric UV violet cuts through — not as decoration, but as a laser does: one clean line of light in the dark.

Typography is deliberate without being loud. Outfit Black at display scale is a geometric grotesque with character — clean and well-made, the kind of type you'd find on a quality leather goods catalog or a well-considered community brand. Not condensed-industrial, not literary serif. Just confident. Inter handles everything else: neutral, humanist, invisible.

Motion is choreographed but fast. Entrances stagger. Sequences are deliberate. Nothing lingers past 250ms. The laser violet appears as glow — box-shadow, not fill — in high-concentration moments: avatar borders, active link cards, focus rings. The amber is the warm constant; the violet is the flash.
keyCharacteristics: Void-black ground with cool violet-tinted surfaces — UV club wall, not leather bar wood
Warm amber glows against cool dark surfaces — the tension between leather and rave is the point
One laser accent: electric UV violet — used as glow and stroke only, never as fill
Outfit Black/ExtraBold at display and headline scale; Inter for all body and UI text
Choreographed but fast: 120–250ms durations, ease-out-quart, laser glow on specific trigger moments
WCAG 2.2 AA minimum; dark-first means high contrast is on-brand, not a trade-off

rules.name: The Three Lights Rule
rules.body: Three light sources, three colors. Amber: the warm bounce off leather hardware. Violet: the UV laser cutting through fog. Crimson: the exit sign, the danger state. No fourth light source. No additional accent colors.

rules.name: The Void Surface Rule
rules.body: The body background is #0a0a0a — achromatic, oklch(0.06 0.000 0), no chroma. The surface tokens carry the cool violet tint. Never put chroma in the bg; it breaks the depth stack.

rules.name: The Cold Room Rule
rules.body: All neutral surfaces tint toward cool violet (hue ~290), not warm amber. The amber primary glows AGAINST the cool ground. Adding warmth to the surfaces dissolves the contrast that makes amber read as amber.

rules.name: The Laser as Glow Rule
rules.body: Electric violet (laser) never fills a card, panel, or button background. It appears exclusively as: (1) box-shadow glow layers, (2) border strokes on focused or active elements, (3) sparse text on large-scale brand moments where font-size ≥ 1rem and font-weight ≥ 600.

rules.name: The Violet Glow Budget
rules.body: At most two violet glows per viewport at any time. If three elements glow violet simultaneously, none read as laser — they read as theme. Laser is specific; specificity is the point.

rules.name: The Dark Text on Amber Rule
rules.body: The amber primary at oklch(0.72 0.145 75) carries dark text (bg) — not white. Contrast is 9.5:1 (WCAG AAA). Hardware labeling, not warning buttons. Don't override.

rules.name: The Outfit Scale Rule
rules.body: Outfit appears only at Display and Headline scale — clamp(1.75rem...) and above. Below that threshold, Inter takes over. Outfit at small sizes loses the geometric clarity that earns its place.

rules.name: The Weight Floor Rule
rules.body: Outfit at weight 700 or below on dark backgrounds starts reading as a generic grotesque. Weights 800 and 900 only — the weight is the character.

rules.name: The Glow-Only Rule
rules.body: Box shadows with dark rgba() are invisible on void-black surfaces and prohibited. State is communicated with amber or violet glow, not shadow depth.

dos: Do keep bg as #0a0a0a — achromatic. The void. Colors live above it.
Do tint all neutral surfaces cool/violet (hue ~290), not warm. Amber glows AGAINST cool surfaces.
Do use laser violet exclusively as glow and stroke — never as fill or background.
Do use Outfit at display and headline scale only (weights 800–900). Below that, switch to Inter.
Do use dark text (bg) on amber fills — 9.5:1 contrast, hardware labeling, intentional.
Do keep violet glows to at most two per viewport. Laser specificity = laser impact.
Do cap motion at 250ms. Choreographed, never theatrical.
Do include prefers-reduced-motion alternatives on every animation.
Do use OKLCH in prose as the canonical reference; hex in code.
donts: Don't use neon colors everywhere, or as background fills, or as gradients. One specific laser color, one specific use — not the synthwave all-over treatment.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text on a gradient). Single solid colors only.
Don't use RGB gradients, purple-to-pink gradients, or multiple neon accents bleeding into each other. That's synthwave.
Don't use Linktree, Beacons, or generic link-in-bio patterns: rounded-pill buttons, pastel fills, gradient rainbow backgrounds.
Don't use Hope UI, Bootstrap-default, or out-of-the-box admin skins.
Don't add glassmorphism (backdrop-filter: blur) as a default card treatment.
Don't use side-stripe borders (border-left or border-right > 1px as a colored accent).
Don't use Outfit below 1.5rem or at weight 700 or below — it loses the geometric clarity that makes it worthwhile.
Don't use box-shadow with dark rgba() on void-black surfaces — invisible.
Don't let violet glow appear on more than two elements per viewport simultaneously.
Don't add tracked all-caps eyebrows above every section.
